correctness.rationale: For every fixed maximal independent set of a cycle, the priority-order certificate is proved in both directions. Conditioning on marks of selected vertices factors all unselected-vertex requirements across gaps of distances 2 and 3, with factors 1-min(s,t) and (1-s)(1-t). Integrating internal selected marks gives G(s,t)>=2H(s,t), because the central expected factor is 2/3 while E[(1-Z)^2]=1/3; shared exterior contributes a common nonnegative factor. The wraparound n=6 case takes t=s. Every n>=8 admits a common exterior of 2/3 gaps; small uniform cycles are transitive on their maximal independent sets. All quantifiers and boundaries checked; a standard-library rational-DP verifier agrees with direct permutation enumeration for n<=8 and checks all cycles n<=15. Finite tests are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating source proves tree-only rigidity and spider formulas, not cycle laws. The density/local-limit source lacks fixed-output cycle probability comparisons. Targeted comparisons to published random-greedy laws on chain, threshold and multipartite graphs reveal different graph classes and observables. Neither published records nor web keyword searches exposed the cycle classification or the six-edge pointwise likelihood-ratio lemma. This supports bounded best-knowledge originality, not a claim of exhaustive worldwide priority.

value.rationale: Uniformity of output over maximal independent sets is a natural sampling-quality question distinct from greedy set size or mere maximal-set counts. Cycles are the canonical vertex-transitive test family, yet have a nontrivial exception C7. The complete classification for every simple cycle and a scale-independent factor-two local probability obstruction constitute a structural result with potential utility for assessing random-priority graph samplers, not a routine table recomputation.
